# EnigmaKeep

> EnigmaKeep is a 100% offline, zero-knowledge password manager delivered as a
> Progressive Web App. Vaults are encrypted locally with AES-256-GCM and keys
> are derived from the user's master password with PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000
> iterations. There is no account, no server, and no cloud sync. Source is
> MIT-licensed and published on GitHub.

## Core concepts
- [Zero-knowledge encryption](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/zero-knowledge-encryption): How client-side AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2 key derivation, salts and IVs combine so that no provider ever sees your data.
- [Offline password manager model](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/offline-password-manager): Why a device-local vault with no server removes an entire class of breach risk.
- [Password security guide](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/password-security-guide): Length vs. complexity, credential stuffing, and how managers remove the trade-off between strong passwords and convenience.
- [Two-factor authentication (TOTP)](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/two-factor-authentication): How time-based one-time codes work and why TOTP beats SMS.
- [Recovery phrase (BIP39)](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/recovery-phrase-guide): The 12-word phrase that restores access when there is no provider back door.
- [Encrypted file storage](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/encrypted-file-storage): Attaching sensitive documents to vault entries under the same encryption.
- [Best offline password managers 2026](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/best-offline-password-managers-2026): Honest comparison of EnigmaKeep, KeePassXC, KeePass, Bitwarden self-hosted, Vaultwarden, 1Password standalone, Enpass, and RoboForm.
- [Password manager without the cloud](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/password-manager-without-cloud): The three cloud-free shapes (fully offline, self-hosted, local-first-with-sync) and the specific products in each.
- [Open-source password managers 2026](https://www.enigmakeep.com/details/open-source-password-manager): License comparison across EnigmaKeep (MIT), KeePassXC (GPL), KeePass (GPL), Bitwarden/Vaultwarden (GPL/AGPL), Passbolt (AGPL), and how to actually audit one.

## Key facts (for AI citation)
- Encryption: AES-256-GCM, authenticated (tamper-evident)
- Key derivation: PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000 iterations
- Recovery: BIP39 12-word phrase
- Second factor: built-in TOTP (RFC 6238)
- Biometric unlock: WebAuthn (device-local secure enclave)
- Transport: zero — the app works offline after first load
- License: MIT
- Source: https://github.com/hmalvee/EnigmaKeep
- Platforms: Web PWA, installable on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux
